migrates_from._note: One-time MOVE into ~/.my-llm-wiki on first launch of the rebuilt app (desktop paths::migrate_legacy). No symlink, no fallback reads — a clean cutover, so any leftover reference to these fails loudly.

capture_toolchain._note: Single machine-readable catalog for capture capability profiles, tool probes, install commands, and mainland-China variants. Skills declare profile ids in registry/skills.json; preflight.py evaluates only the requested profiles. Tool installation is always opt-in.

mcp._note: Single source of truth for Browser MCP registration across hosts (parallel to default_skill_targets). Local Browser access defaults to the suite-owned stdio bridge so loopback never enters a host/system proxy; remote relay access remains native streamable HTTP. Registration argv is stored as arrays so install-browser.py can preserve Windows drive letters, backslashes, spaces, and shell metacharacters without shell parsing. The script proposes each host's own MCP command and runs it only with explicit consent; hosts without a registration CLI receive an exact manual config snippet. MCP is an access form, not the capability itself: CLI fallback remains equivalent.

claude.remote_register_command: claude mcp add --scope user --transport http my-llm-wiki {remote_endpoint} --header "Authorization: Bearer {token}"

hermes.register_note: Local stdio is intentional: Hermes' httpx can route loopback through the macOS system proxy and ignore the bypass list. The suite bridge disables proxies and reads the current Browser port/token at runtime.

codex.register_note: For a remote relay, export its token as LLM_WIKI_WEB_TOKEN and use the remote HTTP recipe. Local access needs no token in host config because the bridge reads the Browser token file at runtime.

agents.register_note: No MCP registration CLI known for this host — use the equivalent CLI fallback (wiki_ops.py browser-search / local-search / read-pages).

workbuddy.register_note: WorkBuddy has no registration CLI, so the user applies the printed JSON to the expanded per-user config path shown by the installer. Local HTTP loopback is deliberately not offered because its client can route it through the system proxy. A remote relay may still use native HTTPS.

first_run._note: Browser port is resolved like the app itself (desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs): port_pref_file > $PORT > default_port. Health probe only needs liveness — an auth-gated response (token required) still proves the server is up.
